newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE needs quotas for foreign labour, say police.
newsitem.headline: UAE needs quotas for foreign labour, say police.

text.p: The United Arab Emirates, where foreigners outnumber nationals by about three to one, needs a fixed quota of foreign workers, a Dubai police report said.
No nationality, no matter the circumstances, should exceed the number of nationals, a police study on UAE demographic security said in newspaper reports on Friday.
Arab labour should replace Asians, the study said, and the number of nationals should equal expatriates within 20 years.
The Gulf Today daily said research had proved the country would depend on foreign workers for at least another 50 years.
There is no official breakdown between nationals and foreigners among the oil country's population of 2.4 million, but officials estimate nationals make up only 25 to 30 percent of the total.

Most expatriates in the UAE are young men from India, Pakistan and other subcontinental countries. There are also large numbers of Filipinos, Palestinians, Lebanese, Egyptians and Sudanese. Britons make up the majority of Westerners.
Hundreds of thousands of Asian workers have flocked to the UAE and other Gulf Arab states since the oil boom of the 1970s.
About 200,000 illegal foreign workers -- nearly 10 percent of the population -- left the country to avoid stiff new immigration laws under a government amnesty last year.
Officials said at the time the crackdown was aimed at "rectifying an imbalance in the population and targeted all nationalities, not a specific one".
UAE authorities said illegal aliens threatened the country's security.
